hints: Focus on comparing the mass of nitrogen in each formula to the total mass of the whole compound.
Calculate the Mr values, about 80 for ammonium nitrate and about 132 for ammonium sulfate, each containing two N atoms of mass 28.
Think about what the ammonium ion, a conjugate acid of a weak base, does in water and whether that adds H+ to the soil.
walkthrough:
**Find which has more nitrogen by mass**

Both salts contain two nitrogen atoms per formula unit, so the lighter compound has the higher percentage. Let's compare their Mr values.

$$M_r(\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3) = 14+4+14+48 = 80$$
$$M_r((\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4) = 28+8+32.1+64 = 132.1$$

**Calculate the percentage of nitrogen**

Mass of nitrogen in one mole of each is $2 \times 14 = 28$ g. Divide by Mr and multiply by 100.

$$\%N \text{ in } \text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3 = \frac{28}{80} \times 100 = 35.0\%$$
$$\%N \text{ in } (\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 = \frac{28}{132.1} \times 100 = 21.2\%$$
So ammonium nitrate has the higher percentage by mass.

**Decide the effect on soil pH**

Both salts supply the $\text{NH}_4^+$ ion. This is the conjugate acid of the weak base ammonia, so it hydrolyses in water to release $\text{H}^+$.

$$\text{NH}_4^+(aq) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_3(aq) + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+(aq)$$

**Combine both conclusions**

Extra $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ makes neutral soil more acidic, so pH decreases. Higher nitrogen is ammonium nitrate plus pH decrease, which matches one row.

options.A: Correct. Ammonium nitrate has Mr 80 versus 132.1 for ammonium sulfate, so with the same 28 g of N per mole it gives 35% N compared to 21.2% N. Both contain NH4+ which acts as an acid in soil, releasing H3O+ and lowering pH.
options.B: Half right but half wrong. Ammonium nitrate does have the higher %N, but pH does not increase. Students choosing this think ammonium salts are alkaline because they contain ammonia, forgetting NH4+ is acidic and donates H+ to soil.
options.C: Wrong on the percentage. Many students guess ammonium sulfate has more N because its formula has two NH4 groups compared to one in NH4NO3, forgetting the nitrate ion also contains N. In fact both have 2 N atoms, so the heavier sulfate has the lower %N.
options.D: Wrong on both parts. Ammonium sulfate has the lower %N (21.2% vs 35%), and ammonium salts do not make soil alkaline. The NH4+ ion acidifies soil, so pH decreases, not increases.
